text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - President Michal Kovac will hold a news conference on Thursday to give his opinion on a crime wave and spreading power of mafia gangs in Slovakia.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.
- Banking supervision experts from 16 central and eastern European central banks will meet at a conference in Bratislava on April 16 and 17.
- Former Transport Minister Alexander Rezes said he planned to become chairman of the supervisory board of steel producer VSZ Kosice.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Only 6,257 apartments were built last year, 100 more than in 1995, but far behind the original, plan of 10,000-12,000 flats.
- Some 4,834 cars were sold in Slovakia in March bringing the total car sales in the first quarter of 1997 to 13,331 units.
- GSM operator Eurotel, a U.S.-Slovak joint-venture, has signed a roaming agreement with Switzerland increasing the number of its roaming partners to five.
- Tatra Banka a.s. has called an annual shareholders' meeting for May 15.

SME - The paper quotes well informed police sources as saying a man called Jozef Skosik has informed police that two bombs found last month on an opposition Cristian Democratic Movement (KDH) public rally were actions of German and U.S. inteligence services aimed to discredit the Slovak ruling coalition.

PRAVDA - The far-right French National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen will visit Slovakia on April 21 to 24 but he will not meet any state officials as he was invited only as a guest by the nationalist Slovak National Party (SNS).
